Each recipe is a whole working page: the markup, every cell, and the reasoning. The code shown **is** the code running on the page, so what you read is what you'd paste into a `.qmd` of your own. They build on one another roughly in this order.

| Recipe | Shows |
|---|---|
| [Function explorer](function-explorer.qmd) | A text field driving a chart; `makeFunction` / `makeDerivative`; a legend overlay toggling traces; `emptyState` and `vm-invalid` for bad input |
| [Step slider with playback](step-slider.qmd) | `ojs-chart-controls` above the chart; an iteration slider with the play button; the chart tween; `renderTable` |
| [ODE with a convergence plot](ode-convergence.qmd) | `makeFunction2` + `eulerSolve` / `rk4Solve`; a Plotly main chart and an Observable Plot log-log chart sharing the theme; `linearRegression` to read off the order |
| [Distribution explorer](distribution-explorer.qmd) | `sampleCurve` for the exact curve, seeded samples through `histogramBins` under it, `alpha` for the fill |
| ["Try an example" dropdown](try-an-example.qmd) | `applyExampleParams`, `data-example-field`, and the one-DOM-listener wiring that avoids the double-fire |
| [Observable Plot in an SVG block](observable-plot.qmd) | `plotOptions`, `ojs-svg-block` for a fullscreen button, colors read at draw time |

Every page starts with the same three lines, which the recipes don't repeat in their explanations:

```js
VM = window.VM
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```

`VM = window.VM` brings the global into OJS's namespace; the other two are the [theme pair](../first-chart.qmd#the-theme-pair).
